Hi Sam — thanks for the traffic file and the call. This is great context.

High-level proposal (short):
1) MAP goals (2 weeks):
   - Validate realistic tokens/$ at demo traffic and at projected steady-state (tokens-per-second and tokens/$ table included).
   - Confirm caching hit-rate and effective batching window meet cost targets (see thresholds below).
   - Measure p95 latency under production-ish concurrency.

2) Key assumptions we will test during evaluation:
   - Baseline prompt+response tokens per session: 350 tokens (prompt avg 120, response avg 230).
   - Default KV/prefix cache hit-rate we assume: 18% for first-pass; target 30% with simple client-side pinning and prefix prefetch.
   - Batching window: 20ms microbatching by default; we will test 5ms and 50ms to show latency vs cost tradeoff.

3) Acceptance gates (pass/fail):
   - Unit cost: tokens/$ must be within 20% of the modeled target (see attached workbook).
   - p95 latency: <420ms for interactive endpoint during your stated peak concurrency.
   - Quality: generated response must meet the evaluation rubric (we'll share a sample of 40 prompts).

4) Deliverables and dates:
   - Mar 21: Redwood delivers cost model + MAP checklist (spreadsheet) and suggested runbook.
   - Mar 23–24: Pilot runs with OptiHealth traffic (you provide final traffic file by Mar 20).
   - Mar 28: Joint review and go/no-go for Reserved capacity/next steps.

I've attached our initial cost assumptions workbook and a MAP checklist. Ben and Karthik are cc'd to add technical details — Ben will outline cache/batching knobs and Karthik will propose quantization/throughput variants.

Would you like us to keep procurement on the loop for the Mar 28 review?

Best,
Mina

Adding a few concrete engineering notes on the assumptions Mina shared so the MAP checklist has actionable checks:

- Caching:
  * We distinguish prefix caching vs full-session KV caching. For this pilot we recommend enabling prefix caching only (lower state and easier client-side pinning).
  * Conservative hit-rate to validate: 20% (we'll accept >=20% as preliminary). If OptiHealth can add a small client-side prefetch for 3 static prefixes we typically see +8–12% hit rate.

- Batching:
  * Default microbatch window: 20ms (targets lower latency). At 20ms batch we estimate 8% token-cost reduction vs no batching for your traffic pattern.
  * 50ms window yields ~22% token-cost reduction but p95 increases by ~70ms in our measurements.

- Quantization and model variant:
  * We'll run two variants: 8-bit quantized open model (lower cost, slightly higher latency) and a float16 model (higher cost, lower latency). We'll include both numbers in the workbook.

- Short checklist items we will validate during the run:
  1) Measured cache hit-rate (server logs) >= 20% or noted mitigation plan.
  2) Effective batching window measured (median batch latency) matches configured window +/- 5ms.
  3) Tokens emitted per session (server side) within 15% of modeled assumption.

If you can confirm you'll provide a single-week CSV with timestamps and endpoint tags (the sample Sam sent looks good) we'll instrument the run to surface cost breakdowns per endpoint.

Ben

Sam / Procurement — good to have the cleaned CSV. Confirming plan and next steps below so we have a succinct MAP that Procurement can slot into Q2:

Condensed MAP (timeline & owners)
- Mar 21 (Redwood): deliver cost workbook + sensitivity tables (tokens/$ vs cache hit-rate vs batching window) + MAP checklist (owner: Mina).
- Mar 23–24 (Joint run): Redwood runs the pilot using OptiHealth sample traffic with two model variants and 3 batching window settings (5ms, 20ms, 50ms). Instrumentation will capture token counts, cache hit-rate, batch-size distribution, and p95 latency by endpoint (owner: Ben).
- Mar 25: internal reporting (Redwood) — preliminary numbers uploaded to the shared Drive link.
- Mar 28: Joint review call to decide: move forward with Reserved capacity pricing or iterate on requests (owner: Mina / OptiHealth procurement).

Acceptance criteria (short):
- Unit cost: baseline tokens/$ within 20% of modeled.
- Cache: measured hit-rate >= 20% OR agreed mitigation plan.
- Latency: p95 for chat_ui < 420ms at peak concurrency.
- Quality: pass on 40 sample prompts per rubric.

Answers to procurement questions:
- p95 delta for chat_ui at 50ms vs 20ms: we expect +60–90ms (depends on batch size distribution); we'll provide exact numbers in the workbook.
- Sensitivity table: included in the workbook — converts hit-rate delta to $ delta per 10k sessions.

Please confirm you have the dates blocked for Mar 23–24 for the run. If procurement wants an expanded checklist (SOC/contract asks), flag items and we'll include them in the Mar 21 deliverable.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Mina
